list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The tetranuclear complex is centrosymmetric and contains two [Nd2KCl5] units linked through two K–Cl bonds. Each Nd is η5-coordinated by a cyclopentadienyl ligand and coordinated by five bridging chlorides and one THF molecule; each Nd has coordination number eight.

synthesis.procedure: Under an argon atmosphere or vacuum using glovebox/Schlenk techniques, a THF solution of potassium benzyl (0.093 g, 0.714 mmol) was slowly added to a THF solution of 1,2-diphenyl-4-(2-methoxyphenyl)cyclopenta-1,3-diene (0.226 g, 0.697 mmol). After stirring 15 min, the resulting potassium cyclopentadienide solution was added dropwise to a stirred suspension of NdCl3(THF)2.5 (0.308 g, 0.714 mmol) in THF (10 mL). After solids dissolved and precipitate began to form, the mixture was stirred overnight and centrifuged (5000 rpm, 10 min). The solution was concentrated under vacuum to approximately 5–7 mL; hexane (35 mL) was carefully layered on top. Bluish crystals formed within one week. Crystals were collected from the mother liquor; remaining crystals were washed with hexane (3 × 5 mL) and dried under dynamic vacuum.
